sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca ko 'parādho mahendrasya kaḥ pramādaś ca sūtaja tapasā vālakhilyānāṃ saṃbhūto garuḍaḥ katham
english: Śaunaka said: What was Mahendra's offence, and what was his blunder, O son of a sūta? And how was Garuḍa born through the austerities of the Vālakhilyas?

sanskrit: kaśyapasya dvijāteś ca kathaṃ vai pakṣirāṭ sutaḥ adhṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānām avadhyaś cābhavat katham
english: And how did the lord of birds become the son of the twice-born Kaśyapa? How did he become unassailable by all beings, and how did he become invincible?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca kāmacārī sa kāmavīryaś ca khecaraḥ etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ purāṇe yadi paṭhyate
english: And how did that sky-traveller move freely at will and possess strength at will? I wish to hear all this, if it is recorded in the Purāṇa.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca viṣayo 'yaṃ purāṇasya yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi śṛṇu me vadataḥ sarvam etat saṃkṣepato dvija
english: The Sūta said: What you ask me about is indeed a subject treated in the Purāṇa. O twice-born, hear from me as I recount it all in brief.

sanskrit: yajataḥ putrakāmasya kaśyapasya prajāpateḥ sāhāyyam ṛṣayo devā gandharvāś ca daduḥ kila
english: When the progenitor Kaśyapa was performing a sacrifice desiring a son, the seers, the gods, and the Gandharvas all rendered him assistance.

sanskrit: tatredhmānayane śakro niyuktaḥ kaśyapena ha munayo vālakhilyāś ca ye cānye devatāgaṇāḥ
english: For the fetching of firewood, Śakra was assigned by Kaśyapa, along with the Vālakhilya sages and whatever other hosts of divinities were present.

sanskrit: śakras tu vīryasadṛśam idhmabhāraṃ giriprabham samudyamyānayām āsa nātikṛcchrād iva prabhuḥ
english: Śakra, the mighty lord, easily lifted a load of firewood equal in size to a mountain, commensurate with his own strength, and bore it forward without much effort.

sanskrit: athāpaśyad ṛṣīn hrasvān aṅguṣṭhodaraparvaṇaḥ palāśavṛntikām ekāṃ sahitān vahataḥ pathi
english: Then on the path he saw the tiny sages, as small as a thumb-joint at the belly, all together carrying a single stalk of a palāśa leaf.

sanskrit: pralīnān sveṣv ivāṅgeṣu nirāhārāṃs tapodhanāḥ kliśyamānān mandabalān goṣpade saṃplutodake
english: Those ascetic-wealthy ones, as though dissolved into their own limbs, without food, afflicted with fatigue, with feeble strength, were struggling in water flooded even in a cow's hoofprint.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca sarvān smayāviṣṭo vīryonmattaḥ puraṃdaraḥ avahasyātyagāc chīghraṃ laṅghayitvāvamanya ca
english: Seized with pride and intoxicated by his own might, Purandara laughed at them all and quickly leaped over them with contempt, dishonoring them.

sanskrit: te 'tha roṣasamāviṣṭāḥ subhṛśaṃ jātamanyavaḥ ārebhire mahat karma tadā śakrabhayaṃkaram
english: Then those sages, utterly seized by rage and deeply angered, undertook a great deed that would strike terror into Śakra.

sanskrit: juhuvus te sutapaso vidhivaj jātavedasam mantrair uccāvacair viprā yena kāmena tac chṛṇu
english: Those brāhmaṇas of intense austerity poured oblations into the sacred fire according to rule, with mantras both high and low, for a particular purpose — hear what that was.

sanskrit: kāmavīryaḥ kāmagamo devarājabhayapradaḥ indro 'nyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ bhaved iti yatavratāḥ
english: "Let there arise another Indra of all the gods — one possessed of strength at will and movement at will, one who strikes fear into the king of the gods" — so vowed those keepers of their vows.

sanskrit: indrāc chataguṇaḥ śaurye vīrye caiva manojavaḥ tapaso naḥ phalenādya dāruṇaḥ saṃbhavatv iti
english: "Let one who is a hundredfold superior to Indra in heroism and prowess, swift as thought, and formidable, now come into being through the fruit of our austerities" — thus they spoke.

sanskrit: tad buddhvā bhṛśasaṃtapto devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ jagāma śaraṇaṃ tatra kaśyapaṃ saṃśitavratam
english: Learning of this, the king of the gods, Śatakratu, greatly distressed, went for refuge to Kaśyapa of sharpened vow.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā devarājasya kaśyapo 'tha prajāpatiḥ vālakhilyān upāgamya karmasiddhim apṛcchata
english: Having heard of the king of the gods' plight, the progenitor Kaśyapa approached the Vālakhilyas and inquired about the completion of their ritual act.

sanskrit: evam astv iti taṃ cāpi pratyūcuḥ satyavādinaḥ tān kaśyapa uvācedaṃ sāntvapūrvaṃ prajāpatiḥ
english: Those truth-speakers replied to him, "So be it." Then the progenitor Kaśyapa spoke these conciliatory words to them.

sanskrit: ayam indras tribhuvane niyogād brahmaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ indrārthaṃ ca bhavanto 'pi yatnavantas tapodhanāḥ
english: "This Indra has been appointed over the three worlds by Brahmā's command, and you too, O wealthy in austerities, have been striving for the sake of Indra."

sanskrit: na mithyā brahmaṇo vākyaṃ kartum arhatha sattamāḥ bhavatāṃ ca na mithyāyaṃ saṃkalpo me cikīrṣitaḥ
english: "O best of beings, you ought not render Brahmā's word false; nor do I intend to make your resolve come to naught."

sanskrit: bhavatv eṣa patatrīṇām indro 'tibalasattvavān prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ caiva devarājasya yācataḥ
english: "Let this one become Indra of the winged beings, supremely powerful and courageous; and let your grace be shown to the king of the gods who now supplicates you."

sanskrit: evam uktāḥ kaśyapena vālakhilyās tapodhanāḥ pratyūcur abhisaṃpūjya muniśreṣṭhaṃ prajāpatim
english: Thus addressed by Kaśyapa, the Vālakhilyas, wealthy in austerities, replied after duly honoring that best of sages and progenitor.

sanskrit: indrārtho 'yaṃ samārambhaḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ prajāpate apatyārthaṃ samārambho bhavataś cāyam īpsitaḥ
english: "This undertaking of ours all together was for the sake of Indra, O Progenitor; and your desired undertaking is for the sake of offspring."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ saphalaṃ karma tvayā vai pratigṛhyatām tathā caiva vidhatsvātra yathā śreyo 'nupaśyasi
english: "So let this fruit-bearing act be accepted by you, and arrange things here as you see to be the greatest good."

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu devī dākṣāyaṇī śubhā vinatā nāma kalyāṇī putrakāmā yaśasvinī
english: At this very time, the goddess Vinatā — the auspicious, beautiful daughter of Dakṣa, that illustrious one who was desirous of sons —

sanskrit: tapas taptvā vrataparā snātā puṃsavane śuciḥ upacakrāma bhartāraṃ tām uvācātha kaśyapaḥ
english: — having performed austerities and being devoted to her vow, having bathed and purified herself in the puṃsavana rite, approached her husband. Then Kaśyapa spoke to her.

sanskrit: ārambhaḥ saphalo devi bhavitāyaṃ tavepsitaḥ janayiṣyasi putrau dvau vīrau tribhuvaneśvarau
english: "This undertaking of yours, O goddess, shall bear the fruit you desired; you will give birth to two heroic sons, lords of the three worlds."

sanskrit: tapasā vālakhilyānāṃ mama saṃkalpajau tathā bhaviṣyato mahābhāgau putrau te lokapūjitau
english: "Born through the austerities of the Vālakhilyas and from my own intention likewise, your two highly fortunate sons shall be worshipped throughout the worlds."

sanskrit: uvāca caināṃ bhagavān mārīcaḥ punar eva ha dhāryatām apramādena garbho 'yaṃ sumahodayaḥ
english: The venerable Mārīca then spoke to her again: "This embryo of great and auspicious potency must be carried with all care and without negligence."

sanskrit: ekaḥ sarvapatatrīṇām indratvaṃ kārayiṣyati lokasaṃbhāvito vīraḥ kāmavīryo vihaṃgamaḥ
english: "One of them, that heroic sky-ranger honoured throughout the worlds, possessed of strength at will, shall exercise the lordship of Indra over all winged creatures."

sanskrit: śatakratum athovāca prīyamāṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ tvatsahāyau khagāv etau bhrātarau te bhaviṣyataḥ
english: Then the progenitor, pleased, spoke to Śatakratu: "These two birds shall be your brothers and allies."

sanskrit: naitābhyāṃ bhavitā doṣaḥ sakāśāt te puraṃdara vyetu te śakra saṃtāpas tvam evendro bhaviṣyasi
english: "No harm shall come to you from these two, O Purandara. Let your anxiety depart, O Śakra; you yourself shall remain Indra."

sanskrit: na cāpy evaṃ tvayā bhūyaḥ kṣeptavyā brahmavādinaḥ na cāvamānyā darpāt te vāgviṣā bhṛśakopanāḥ
english: "And you must never again despise the knowers of Brahman, nor out of arrogance dishonor those whose words are venomous and who are provoked to fierce anger."

sanskrit: evam ukto jagāmendro nirviśaṅkas triviṣṭapam vinatā cāpi siddhārthā babhūva muditā tadā
english: Thus addressed, Indra departed free of anxiety to heaven, and Vinatā too had her purpose accomplished and became joyful.

sanskrit: janayām āsa putrau dvāv aruṇaṃ garuḍaṃ tathā aruṇas tayos tu vikala ādityasya puraḥsaraḥ
english: She gave birth to two sons — Aruṇa and Garuḍa. Of the two, Aruṇa was deformed and became the forerunner of the Sun.

sanskrit: patatrīṇāṃ tu garuḍa indratvenābhyaṣicyata tasyaitat karma sumahac chrūyatāṃ bhṛgunandana
english: Garuḍa was consecrated as Indra of the winged beings. O joy of the Bhṛgu line, hear now of this great deed of his.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tatas tasmin dvijaśreṣṭha samudīrṇe tathāvidhe garutmān pakṣirāṭ tūrṇaṃ saṃprāpto vibudhān prati
english: The Sūta said: Then, O best of the twice-born, when that event had thus unfolded, Garutmān, the lord of birds, swiftly advanced against the gods.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvātibalaṃ caiva prākampanta samantataḥ parasparaṃ ca pratyaghnan sarvapraharaṇāny api
english: Seeing him of such overwhelming strength, they trembled on all sides; and yet they struck one another even while wielding all their weapons.

sanskrit: tatra cāsīd ameyātmā vidyudagnisamaprabhaḥ bhauvanaḥ sumahāvīryaḥ somasya parirakṣitā
english: There was present one of immeasurable spirit, blazing like lightning and fire, named Bhauvana, of very great heroism, the guardian of the Soma.

sanskrit: sa tena patagendreṇa pakṣatuṇḍanakhaiḥ kṣataḥ muhūrtam atulaṃ yuddhaṃ kṛtvā vinihato yudhi
english: Wounded by that lord of birds with his wings, beak, and talons, he fought an incomparable battle for a moment and then was slain in combat.

sanskrit: rajaś coddhūya sumahat pakṣavātena khecaraḥ kṛtvā lokān nirālokāṃs tena devān avākirat
english: The sky-traveller stirred up a great mass of dust with the wind of his wings, darkened the worlds so they were without light, and with it scattered the gods.

sanskrit: tenāvakīrṇā rajasā devā moham upāgaman na cainaṃ dadṛśuś channā rajasāmṛtarakṣiṇaḥ
english: Enveloped in that dust, the gods fell into confusion; the guardians of the nectar, shrouded by the dust, could not see him.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃloḍayām āsa garuḍas tridivālayam pakṣatuṇḍaprahāraiś ca devān sa vidadāra ha
english: Thus Garuḍa threw the abode of the three heavens into turmoil, and with blows of his wings and beak he tore the gods asunder.

sanskrit: tato devaḥ sahasrākṣas tūrṇaṃ vāyum acodayat vikṣipemāṃ rajovṛṣṭiṃ tavaitat karma māruta
english: Then the thousand-eyed god quickly urged on the Wind: "Disperse this rain of dust — that is your task, O Wind."

sanskrit: atha vāyur apovāha tad rajas tarasā balī tato vitimire jāte devāḥ śakunim ārdayan
english: Then the mighty Wind swiftly blew away that dust. Once the darkness had cleared, the gods assailed the bird.

sanskrit: nanāda coccair balavān mahāmegharavaḥ khagaḥ vadhyamānaḥ suragaṇaiḥ sarvabhūtāni bhīṣayan utpapāta mahāvīryaḥ pakṣirāṭ paravīrahā
english: The powerful bird roared aloud with the sound of a great storm-cloud, terrifying all beings even while being assailed by the hosts of gods; and the lord of birds, of great heroism and slayer of enemy heroes, soared upward.

sanskrit: tam utpatyāntarikṣasthaṃ devānām upari sthitam varmiṇo vibudhāḥ sarve nānāśastrair avākiran
english: Soaring up and hovering above the gods in the midair, all the armoured gods showered him with weapons of every kind from below.

sanskrit: paṭṭiśaiḥ parighaiḥ śūlair gadābhiś ca savāsavāḥ kṣurāntair jvalitaiś cāpi cakrair ādityarūpibhiḥ
english: With axes, iron clubs, spears, and maces together with Vāsava, and also with blazing discuses with sharp edges resembling the sun in form.

sanskrit: nānāśastravisargaiś ca vadhyamānaḥ samantataḥ kurvan sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ pakṣirāṇ na vyakampata
english: Though struck on all sides by discharges of every kind of weapon and waging a most tumultuous battle, the lord of birds did not waver.

sanskrit: vinardann iva cākāśe vainateyaḥ pratāpavān pakṣābhyām urasā caiva samantād vyākṣipat surān
english: Roaring as if filling the sky, the valiant son of Vinatā flung the gods in every direction with his wings and chest.

sanskrit: te vikṣiptās tato devāḥ prajagmur garuḍārditāḥ nakhatuṇḍakṣatāś caiva susruvuḥ śoṇitaṃ bahu
english: Those gods, thus hurled away and tormented by Garuḍa, fled; wounded by his talons and beak, they bled profusely.

sanskrit: sādhyāḥ prācīṃ sagandharvā vasavo dakṣiṇāṃ diśam prajagmuḥ sahitā rudraiḥ patagendrapradharṣitāḥ
english: The Sādhyas along with the Gandharvas fled to the east; the Vasus fled to the south along with the Rudras, all driven away by the lord of birds.

sanskrit: diśaṃ pratīcīm ādityā nāsatyā uttarāṃ diśam muhur muhuḥ prekṣamāṇā yudhyamānā mahaujasam
english: The Ādityas fled to the western quarter, the Nāsatyas to the north, repeatedly glancing back and fighting against the one of great might.

sanskrit: aśvakrandena vīreṇa reṇukena ca pakṣiṇā krathanena ca śūreṇa tapanena ca khecaraḥ
english: With the hero Aśvakranda, with the bird Reṇuka, with the valiant Krathana, and with the sky-traveller Tapana —

sanskrit: ulūkaśvasanābhyāṃ ca nimeṣeṇa ca pakṣiṇā prarujena ca saṃyuddhaṃ cakāra pralihena ca
english: — and with Ulūka and Śvasana, and with the bird Nimeṣa, and with Praruja and Praliha — with all these he waged battle.

sanskrit: tān pakṣanakhatuṇḍāgrair abhinad vinatāsutaḥ yugāntakāle saṃkruddhaḥ pinākīva mahābalaḥ
english: With tips of his wings, talons, and beak the son of Vinatā tore them apart, infuriated like Śiva with his Pināka bow at the end of an age, possessed of great might.

sanskrit: mahāvīryā mahotsāhās tena te bahudhā kṣatāḥ rejur abhraghanaprakhyā rudhiraughapravarṣiṇaḥ
english: Those beings of great heroism and great energy, lacerated in many ways by him, shone like dense storm clouds raining torrents of blood.

sanskrit: tān kṛtvā patagaśreṣṭhaḥ sarvān utkrāntajīvitān atikrānto 'mṛtasyārthe sarvato 'gnim apaśyata
english: Having left all those beings deprived of their lives, the best of birds, advancing for the sake of the nectar, saw fire blazing on all sides.

sanskrit: āvṛṇvānaṃ mahājvālam arcirbhiḥ sarvato 'mbaram dahantam iva tīkṣṇāṃśuṃ ghoraṃ vāyusamīritam
english: It was enveloping the sky on all sides with its great flames, scorching like the fierce-rayed sun, terrible, fanned by the wind.

sanskrit: tato navatyā navatīr mukhānāṃ; kṛtvā tarasvī garuḍo mahātmā nadīḥ samāpīya mukhais tatas taiḥ; suśīghram āgamya punar javena
english: Then the swift and great-souled Garuḍa, having made ninety times ninety mouths, drank up rivers with those mouths and returned again with great speed.

sanskrit: jvalantam agniṃ tam amitratāpanaḥ; samāstarat patraratho nadībhiḥ tataḥ pracakre vapur anyad alpaṃ; praveṣṭukāmo 'gnim abhipraśāmya
english: That scorcher of enemies, the chariot of feathers, extinguished the blazing fire with those rivers. Then, wishing to enter and having quenched the fire, he assumed a different, small form.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca jāmbūnadamayo bhūtvā marīcivikacojjvalaḥ praviveśa balāt pakṣī vārivega ivārṇavam
english: The Sūta said: Becoming made of pure gold, blazing brilliantly with rays of light, the bird forcefully entered like a current of water rushing into the ocean.

sanskrit: sa cakraṃ kṣuraparyantam apaśyad amṛtāntike paribhramantam aniśaṃ tīkṣṇadhāram ayasmayam
english: He saw near the nectar a wheel rimmed with razor-sharp blades, whirling ceaselessly, of keen edge, made of iron.

sanskrit: jvalanārkaprabhaṃ ghoraṃ chedanaṃ somahāriṇām ghorarūpaṃ tad atyarthaṃ yantraṃ devaiḥ sunirmitam
english: Blazing with the radiance of fire and sun, terrible, a cutter-down of those who would steal the Soma — that device of most terrible form had been skillfully constructed by the gods.

sanskrit: tasyāntaraṃ sa dṛṣṭvaiva paryavartata khecaraḥ arāntareṇābhyapatat saṃkṣipyāṅgaṃ kṣaṇena ha
english: The sky-traveller, perceiving the gaps in it, began to revolve; contracting his body in an instant, he darted through the spaces between the spokes.

sanskrit: adhaś cakrasya caivātra dīptānalasamadyutī vidyujjihvau mahāghorau dīptāsyau dīptalocanau
english: Below the wheel, in that place, were two serpents of most fearsome kind — their tongues like lightning, their faces blazing, their eyes blazing — shining with the radiance of a blazing fire.

sanskrit: cakṣurviṣau mahāvīryau nityakruddhau tarasvinau rakṣārtham evāmṛtasya dadarśa bhujagottamau
english: Those best of serpents, possessed of poison in their very gaze, of great heroism, perpetually enraged, and swift — he saw them stationed there for the very purpose of guarding the nectar.

sanskrit: sadā saṃrabdhanayanau sadā cānimiṣekṣaṇau tayor eko 'pi yaṃ paśyet sa tūrṇaṃ bhasmasād bhavet
english: Their eyes always inflamed, their gaze forever unwinking — whomever even one of the two looked upon would instantly be reduced to ashes.

sanskrit: tayoś cakṣūṃṣi rajasā suparṇas tūrṇam āvṛṇot adṛṣṭarūpas tau cāpi sarvataḥ paryakālayat
english: Suparṇa swiftly blinded the eyes of the two with dust; his own form unseen, he then assailed them on all sides.

sanskrit: tayor aṅge samākramya vainateyo 'ntarikṣagaḥ ācchinat tarasā madhye somam abhyadravat tataḥ
english: Mounting upon the bodies of the two, the sky-ranger, son of Vinatā, swiftly cut them down in the middle; then he rushed toward the Soma.

sanskrit: samutpāṭyāmṛtaṃ tat tu vainateyas tato balī utpapāta javenaiva yantram unmathya vīryavān
english: That powerful and heroic son of Vinatā then tore out the nectar, and having shattered the device, he leaped upward with great speed.

sanskrit: apītvaivāmṛtaṃ pakṣī parigṛhyāśu vīryavān agacchad apariśrānta āvāryārkaprabhāṃ khagaḥ
english: Without drinking the nectar, the powerful bird, swiftly grasping it, departed without fatigue — that sky-traveller who was able to obscure the brilliance of the sun.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā tu tadākāśe vainateyaḥ sameyivān tasya nārāyaṇas tuṣṭas tenālaulyena karmaṇā
english: Then in the sky the son of Vinatā met Viṣṇu; Nārāyaṇa was pleased with him for that act of freedom from greed.

sanskrit: tam uvācāvyayo devo varado 'smīti khecaram sa vavre tava tiṣṭheyam uparīty antarikṣagaḥ
english: The imperishable god said to that sky-traveller, "I am a granter of boons." That sky-ranger chose: "May I always dwell above you."

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ bhūyo 'pi nārāyaṇam idaṃ vacaḥ ajaraś cāmaraś ca syām amṛtena vināpy aham
english: And he spoke these words to Nārāyaṇa once more: "May I be free from old age and immortal even without the nectar."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya varau tau ca garuḍo viṣṇum abravīt bhavate 'pi varaṃ dadmi vṛṇītāṃ bhagavān api
english: Having received those two boons, Garuḍa said to Viṣṇu: "I also grant a boon to you; let the Blessed Lord choose as well."

sanskrit: taṃ vavre vāhanaṃ kṛṣṇo garutmantaṃ mahābalam dhvajaṃ ca cakre bhagavān upari sthāsyasīti tam
english: Kṛṣṇa chose the mighty Garutmān as his mount; and the Blessed Lord made him his banner, saying to him: "You shall abide above me."

sanskrit: anupatya khagaṃ tv indro vajreṇāṅge 'bhyatāḍayat vihaṃgamaṃ surāmitraṃ harantam amṛtaṃ balāt
english: Chasing the bird, Indra struck him on the body with his vajra — that sky-ranger, that enemy of the gods, who was carrying away the nectar by force.

sanskrit: tam uvācendram ākrande garuḍaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ prahasañ ślakṣṇayā vācā tathā vajrasamāhataḥ
english: Thus struck by the vajra, Garuḍa, the best of fliers, spoke to Indra with a laugh and with gentle words:

sanskrit: ṛṣer mānaṃ kariṣyāmi vajraṃ yasyāsthisaṃbhavam vajrasya ca kariṣyāmi tava caiva śatakrato
english: "I shall honor the sage from whose bones the vajra was made; and I shall show honour to the vajra itself and to you as well, O Śatakratu."

sanskrit: eṣa patraṃ tyajāmy ekaṃ yasyāntaṃ nopalapsyase na hi vajranipātena rujā me 'sti kadā cana
english: "I now shed a single feather the end of which you shall never find; for the fall of the vajra has never caused me any pain at any time."
